past.date: Wed 29 Jul 2026, after the US close (Thu 30 Jul, about 4am Singapore)
past.vs: Revenue $90.0bn, +18% vs a year earlier, vs $87.6bn consensus (Reuters/Visible Alpha): +2.7% beat. EPS $4.81 reported; $4.74 excluding OpenAI vs $4.24 expected (+11.8%). Azure +43% (also +43% excluding currency) vs about 40% expected and Microsoft's own 39-40% guide.
past.guide: September quarter: revenue $89.85-90.95bn (+15.7% to +17.1% vs $77.7bn a year earlier; midpoint +16.4%) vs about $89.7bn consensus (+15.5%); Azure about +45% in constant currency vs about 41% expected.
past.reaction: Shares +15.5% on 30 Jul ($451.10 vs $390.54), Microsoft's biggest one-day gain since 2008 (about $450bn of market value).
take: Azure accelerated. +43% vs +40% in the March quarter and +39% in December (each vs a year earlier); guided to about +45% for September.
Still short of capacity. Demand exceeds the data-centre capacity Microsoft has; no end date given.

Capex keeps rising. $41bn in the quarter including finance leases; over $50bn guided for September. The calendar-2026 plan was cut to about $175bn from $190bn because more data-centre leases are now operating leases, which Microsoft does not count as capex; the CFO said spending plans are unchanged. Data-centre buildings are also now depreciated over 25 years instead of 15 (profit effect 'minimal', per the CFO).
Copilot is selling. Over 30m paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats (20m+ in March); net new seats more than doubled vs the March quarter.

Backlog is OpenAI-heavy. Contracted future revenue (RPO) $678bn, +84%; excluding OpenAI +25%. OpenAI was $24.1bn of FY26 revenue, 7.3% of the total (annual report); a broker (BNP Paribas) estimates about 23% of Azure.
Margins slipping slowly. Gross margin 67.2% vs 68.6% a year earlier; FY27 operating margin guided down by less than 1 point.
Cash. Free cash flow $19.6bn in the quarter on $55.4bn operating cash flow.
past.impact: Demand indicators mostly strong (DM4a, DM5 bullish; DM4b neutral at 14% constant currency); guidance only 0.9 points above consensus (DM3 neutral); capex pressure shows in chain C1.

lead: Microsoft is Building history (today's zone: Buy), at +35 on a −100 to +100 scale, down from +39 on 7 Oct and 5 points above the Buy line. The fall came from the liquidity score dropping to 0 from +27: up-day vs down-day volume slipped to 1.30x, just under the 1.3x bullish line, which outweighed Fed rate expectations turning bullish (the chance of a Fed rate rise is now 16%, from 34% a month earlier). Cloud demand and the share-price trend are strong, but the stock costs more than its cloud peers and the dollar is working against it. Caution: over the last 5 years, Buy readings driven by Microsoft's price trend were followed by it lagging the S&P 500 by 8-14 points over the next 6 months.
bullets: Demand is strong but not universal. Demand scores +49 (unchanged): Azure grew 43% in the June quarter vs a year earlier, excluding currency, beating Microsoft's own 39-40% guide (bullish at the guide midpoint, 39.5%; the September guide is about 45%), and AWS plus Google Cloud together grew 50.6% (line: 30%). Analysts' EPS forecast for the year to June 2028 is up 4.9% in 90 days ($23.68 vs $22.58, unchanged from 7 Oct); measured over the next 12 months as the plan intends, it was about +2.8% and neutral on 6 Oct (not recomputed since; engine fix pending). Neutral: Microsoft 365 commercial cloud +14% excluding currency (line: 15%), revenue +17.7% vs a 17.9% average for the prior four quarters, gross margin 67.9% over the last 4 quarters vs 68.8% for the 4 before, and September guidance (+16.4%) only 0.9 points above the +15.5% expected.

It is dearer than its cloud peers. Valuation scores −28 (unchanged): 25.1x next-12-month earnings vs 21.4x for the median of Amazon, Alphabet and Oracle (+17%; expensive only at +25%), 38% above them after allowing for growth (1.7 vs 1.2), and 19% above on EV/EBITDA (20.2x vs 17.0x). Against its own history it is not expensive: 29.1x last-12-month earnings vs a 33.9x 5-year median (−14%), though a one-off OpenAI gain flatters last-12-month earnings.

The price trend is as strong as it gets, and that is the least reliable part. Price trend scores +100 (unchanged): $522.61 (−1.35% on the day vs −0.47% for the S&P 500) is 20.5% above its 200-day average, the 50-day average is 15.0% above the 200-day, and the 3-month return is 36.8 points ahead of the three cloud peers. Against it, the dollar index is 3.05 points higher than 20 trading days earlier (bearish at +1). In its favour, markets price a 16% chance of a Fed rate rise on 28 Oct, down from 34% a month earlier (a 17.0-point shift towards cuts, now past the 15 points needed to count; a cut is priced at about 1%). AZR.sells: Azure cloud computing and AI capacity, plus server software (SQL Server, Windows Server) and GitHub.
AZR.buyers: Companies, governments and AI labs (OpenAI the largest), mostly on pay-as-you-use or multi-year contracts.
pos: Biggest and fastest-growing part: about 39% of sales and +31% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 quarters before (Azure alone +43% in the June quarter).
Contracted backlog of $678bn (all commercial, Jun-26) gives years of visibility.
Usage-based: grows as customers run more AI workloads, without new licence sales.
neg: Earns below the company's segment operating margin: Intelligent Cloud 41% vs about 47% for all segments (last 4 quarters), and slipping as AI capacity costs rise.
Needs about $175bn of capex in calendar 2026 (including leases); payback depends on growth staying high.
Concentrated: OpenAI was 7.3% of all FY26 revenue (annual report) and an estimated ~23% of Azure (broker estimate).

ENT.sells: Enterprise support contracts, consulting and partner services.
neg: Small (about 2.5% of sales) and slow-growing (+7% vs a year earlier, last 4 quarters).
Shares Intelligent Cloud's margin, which is falling.

M365.sells: Office, Teams, Exchange, security and Copilot subscriptions sold to companies (per user, per month).
M365.buyers: Businesses and public bodies worldwide; over 30m paid Copilot seats (Jun-26).
pos: Recurring subscriptions: about 31% of sales, +16% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before (Microsoft 365 commercial cloud alone +14% in the June quarter, excluding currency).
Earns the highest margin: Productivity and Business Processes 60% segment operating margin (last 4 quarters), up from 58% a year earlier.
Copilot adds a price uplift on an installed base of hundreds of millions of users.
neg: Growth depends on price rises and Copilot add-ons more than new users.
AI tools from rivals (Google, Anthropic, OpenAI) threaten to change how office work is done: the Feb-26 software sell-off was about this.
Seat counts are tied to employment at customers.

LNK.sells: LinkedIn premium subscriptions, recruiting tools and advertising.
pos: +11% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before; unique professional data.
neg: Recruiting revenue swings with the hiring cycle.
Advertising part competes with Google and Meta.

DYC.sells: Dynamics business software (finance, sales, customer service) and Microsoft 365 subscriptions for households.
DYC.buyers: Mid-size and large companies (Dynamics); consumers (Microsoft 365 Personal/Family).
pos: Fastest growth in the Productivity segment: +19% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before.
neg: Dynamics competes with Salesforce, SAP and Oracle.

MPC.sells: Windows licences for PC makers, Surface devices, Xbox consoles, games and Game Pass, and Bing/news advertising.
MPC.buyers: PC makers, consumers, gamers and advertisers.
pos: Search advertising and Windows still generate cash.
Xbox content (incl. Activision) is a large library.
neg: Shrinking: about 16% of sales vs 19% a year earlier; revenue -1% over the last 4 quarters vs the 4 before (June quarter -4%).
Lowest margin: 27% segment operating margin (last 4 quarters).
Not recurring: depends on PC and console cycles.

shift.title: What the shift means for Microsoft
pos: Sales are moving towards cloud and subscriptions: Azure & server products rose from about 35% to 39% of sales in a year (last 4 quarters vs the 4 a year earlier), and the low-margin personal computing segment fell from 19% to 16%.
The mix shift on its own added about 0.4 points to segment operating margin vs a year earlier, because personal computing (27% margin) shrank.
More of revenue is contracted or subscription-based, which makes earnings steadier.
neg: The fastest-growing part (Azure & server products, +31%) earns below the company's segment margin (41% vs about 47%), and its margin is falling as AI capacity costs rise.
Growth now depends heavily on AI demand, much of it from one customer (OpenAI).
Capex is growing faster than operating cash: free cash flow was $67.0bn over the 12 months to Jun 2026 (excluding finance-lease data centres), while cash capex was $116.0bn.
